title: Lab 1A — KMS + S3 encryption
topic: CMK key policies vs IAM, SSE-KMS vs SSE-S3, Bucket Key, envelope encryption, simulate-principal-policy on kms:Decrypt
format: 10 timed scenario questions (~16 min, ~96 sec each). Reinforces Night 2 SSE-KMS lab on witcoskitech.com study-lab/kms-test/ prefix. Answer without night-2-quiz-answers.json first.
answerDistribution: A×2 B×3 C×3 D×2 — options shuffled so correct letter varies

questions.question: Night 2 lab: witcoskitech.com bucket default encryption is SSE-S3 (AES256). Objects under study-lab/kms-test/ use SSE-KMS with alias/saa-study-witcoskitech. A reader gets AccessDenied on one kms-test object. What must be true for READ access?

options.A: Only s3:GetObject on the bucket — SSE-KMS objects decrypt automatically
options.B: s3:GetObject on the object plus kms:Decrypt on the CMK used to encrypt it
options.C: kms:Encrypt on the CMK plus s3:ListBucket on the whole bucket
options.D: CloudFront OAC on the distribution — KMS permissions are not required

questions.question: A developer uploads to study-lab/kms-test/ with aws s3 cp --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id alias/saa-study-witcoskitech. github-actions-globalskiatlas simulate shows implicitDeny on kms:Decrypt. What is the likely gap?

options.A: The deploy IAM policy lacks kms:Decrypt (and often s3:GetObject) on that CMK and prefix
options.B: SSE-KMS requires a dedicated S3 VPC endpoint in every VPC
options.C: Bucket default encryption must be changed to SSE-KMS for the whole bucket first
options.D: CloudTrail must log data events before KMS grants decrypt permissions

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares SSE-S3 and SSE-KMS for objects in the same bucket?

options.A: SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys; SSE-KMS uses a KMS CMK with separate key policy and IAM controls
options.B: SSE-S3 requires a customer CMK in every Region; SSE-S3 is deprecated
options.C: SSE-KMS cannot coexist with SSE-S3 objects in one bucket
options.D: SSE-S3 provides CloudTrail data events for every key usage; SSE-KMS does not

questions.question: You enable S3 Bucket Key on a bucket using SSE-KMS. What is the primary benefit?

options.A: Eliminates the need for kms:Decrypt on readers entirely
options.B: Reduces KMS API request costs by using a bucket-level key for SSE-KMS objects
options.C: Automatically rotates the CMK every 24 hours without AWS KMS support
options.D: Replaces CloudFront OAC for private S3 origin access

questions.question: Account B must decrypt objects encrypted with Account A's CMK. Which two policy layers typically need to allow decrypt?

options.A: S3 bucket policy only — KMS key policy is not evaluated for cross-account S3
options.B: KMS key policy in Account A plus IAM policy on Account B's principal
options.C: IAM policy in Account A only — cross-account decrypt never uses key policy
options.D: AWS Organizations SCP in Account B only — KMS ignores resource policies

questions.question: A new CMK is created with alias/saa-study-witcoskitech. The default key policy grants the account root full access. Why keep the root statement?

options.A: Root is required so IAM policies in the account can delegate CMK use to roles and users
options.B: Root statement disables automatic key rotation permanently
options.C: Without root, SSE-S3 default encryption cannot be enabled on any bucket
options.D: Root replaces the need for bucket policies on encrypted prefixes

questions.question: An auditor asks where envelope encryption happens when S3 stores an SSE-KMS object. What is the accurate answer?

options.A: S3 generates a data key; KMS encrypts that data key; S3 stores ciphertext object plus encrypted data key
options.B: KMS stores the entire object ciphertext inside the CMK material
options.C: CloudFront edge locations hold the plaintext object key in memory forever
options.D: IAM encrypts the object at the client before upload using simulate-principal-policy

questions.question: You want a bucket policy that denies any s3:PutObject unless the request uses aws:kms with a specific CMK ARN. Which condition key helps?

options.B: kms:ViaService only — bucket policies cannot inspect encryption headers
options.C: aws:PrincipalOrgID — encryption type is always org-wide
options.D: cloudfront:ViewerCountry — geo block replaces encryption enforcement

questions.question: Night 2 contrast: which service stores encryption keys vs which stores application secrets like Cognito client IDs?

options.A: Secrets Manager stores CMKs; KMS stores Cognito client secrets
options.B: KMS manages encryption keys; Secrets Manager stores secret values (passwords, API keys, config JSON)
options.C: Both services store only IAM access keys for GitHub Actions
options.D: SSM Parameter Store replaces KMS for all SSE-KMS workloads

questions.question: CloudTrail logs show kms:Decrypt from the wiki Lambda role on alias/saa-study-witcoskitech. The role also needs GetSecretValue on a Secrets Manager secret encrypted with that CMK. Why both permissions?

options.A: Secrets Manager returns ciphertext; Lambda must call kms:Decrypt to read the secret value
options.B: GetSecretValue automatically grants kms:Encrypt but never kms:Decrypt
options.C: KMS decrypt is only needed for S3 objects, not Secrets Manager
options.D: CMK alias changes every invoke so decrypt must be re-authorized each time
